Does a Pool Really Add $50,000 to Your Tucson Home?

In a Tucson summer, a swimming pool can feel priceless.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

Does a pool add a fixed amount?Look for evidence in comparable salesBalance enjoyment with resale expectationsMore in Home Improvements ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

If you are adding a pool mainly for your own enjoyment, that can be a perfectly good reason. If you are doing it strictly to increase resale value, study your neighborhood first and avoid assuming a dollar-for-dollar return.

Does a pool add a fixed amount?

In a Tucson summer, a swimming pool can feel priceless. But does it really add $50,000 to your home’s value? Not necessarily. One of the biggest surprises for homeowners is that the cost of installing a feature and the amount buyers will pay for it are two very different numbers.

Look for evidence in comparable sales

Appraisers look for evidence in comparable sales: how similar homes with pools perform against similar homes without them. The result can vary by neighborhood, price range, pool condition, and buyer expectations. A well-maintained pool may be a selling point in one part of the market, while buyers elsewhere may focus on upkeep, water use, insurance, or safety. An expensive custom pool does not automatically deliver an equally expensive resale premium.

Balance enjoyment with resale expectations

If you are adding a pool mainly for your own enjoyment, that can be a perfectly good reason. If you are doing it strictly to increase resale value, study your neighborhood first and avoid assuming a dollar-for-dollar return. For sellers and buyers, an independent appraisal can help separate a home’s amenities from the price the market actually supports.
